title: Fifty Years (Chas and Wilma McIvor)
style: folk country acoustic guitar warm duet male female vocal 96bpm brushed drums gentle storytelling intimate family love Perth Zimbabwe anniversary
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — Chas]
Fifty years is not a round number — it's a fact
An accumulated particular of every act
Of kindness and of patience and of showing up again
Fifty years is the arithmetic of the why and when

[Verse 2 — Wilma]
Fifty years is the garden in October and the rain
The three boys leaving and the house made small again
The Zimbabwe that we carry in the blood and in the name
The Perth that holds us now and holds us all the same

[Chorus — Both]
Fifty years, fifty years
More than either of us ever thought we'd manage
Fifty years, fifty years
Through the seasons and the farm and the language
Fifty years of Sunday mornings and the kettle and the bird
Fifty years of knowing what we mean without a word
The gardens still growing
That's my boy

[Bridge — Chas]
I'd do it again — that's the only honest thing to say
And I'd do it the same way except the parts where I'd convey
A little more of what I knew but didn't say in time
The fifty years gave me the vocabulary for the rhyme

[Outro — Both voices]
Fifty years… the garden knows… the birds know… we know…
The gardens still growing
